insight: Discovery ≠ Conversion — Trust is the real decision driver in activity classes
evidence: Word of mouth is the strongest and most trusted channel
Parents rely on recommendations, child feedback, and observation
Marketing brings leads but not conversions

insight: Enrollment decisions are driven more by convenience and child comfort than objective quality
evidence: Parents prefer nearby classes over better but distant ones
Decision factors include location, timing, and comfort
Process is: trial → child interest → final decision

insight: The real problem is not just discovery — it is inefficient day-to-day operations across the ecosystem
evidence: No structured systems for payments, attendance, or data tracking
Heavy reliance on manual processes (registers, WhatsApp, Excel)
High chances of human error and time-consuming admin tasks

insight: The biggest challenge for platforms like EnrolMe is behavioral adoption, not technological capability
evidence: Institutes show resistance to adopting new systems
Existing workflows are hard to change
Learning new tools is seen as effortful

insight: The ecosystem is highly fragmented, creating a strong opportunity for a centralized platform
evidence: Information is scattered across WhatsApp, teachers, and platforms
No unified way to manage multiple classes
Market is highly fragmented and not easily discoverable

insight: Users do not yet perceive enough pain to demand a solution, making value communication critical
evidence: Parents are willing to pay only a small amount
Platform is seen as “nice to have” not urgent
Current system is messy but still manageable
